column11: Sandostatin, CMS Medicare Part D 2024 (drug_demand): $196,939.32 over 35 beneficiaries = $5,626.84 per beneficiary a year. This is the figure the dossier prints and the book's convention on a CMS series. It describes Sandostatin Injection, the immediate-release subcutaneous product dispensed through the pharmacy benefit; the depot form is a separate asset in the book (Sandostatin Lar, asset 628) and is billed under Part B, where CMS's October 2026 payment limit file puts HCPCS J2353, 'octreotide injection, depot', at $211.321 a mg, or $55,113 a year at the labelled maintenance dose of 20 mg every four weeks (NDA 021008, section 2.2)
column12: the weakest price in this set and it should be read as such. The denominator is 35 Medicare beneficiaries, the series has fallen from 51 in 2020, and octreotide has been multisource for years, so this is a generic-era immediate-release price on a tiny sample. It is also not the price of the product that carries the franchise: almost all Sandostatin revenue is the LAR depot. The J2353 figure above is shown so a reader can see the gap, which is tenfold, and it is deliberately not used as this asset's value because it belongs to a different asset id and the book must not hold two prices for one drug
